issues: Whether a series of transactions constitutes an avoidance transaction under the GAAR
How abuse or misuse of the Income Tax Act's provisions is assessed for GAAR purposes
What is the object, spirit and purpose of the specific provisions relied upon in the transactions
Whether the transactions frustrate or defeat the underlying rationale of the provisions relied upon despite literal compliance
Who bears the burden of proof on the abuse/misuse analysis under GAAR
What is the appropriate standard of review on appeal of a GAAR determination
key_facts: A corporate group carried out a series of transactions
The transactions technically complied with the literal wording of the Income Tax Act
The only real effect of the transactions was to eliminate or reduce tax otherwise payable
CRA has invoked the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) in response
causes_of_action: Application/assessment under the general anti-avoidance rule (section 245, Income Tax Act)
candidate_statutes: Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c 1 (5th Supp), s 245 (GAAR)
Income Tax Act - specific provisions relied upon in the impugned transactions (e.g., relevant deduction, rollover, or attribution provisions)
search_terms: misuse or abuse Income Tax Act
textual contextual and purposive analysis tax
